claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion resistance compared with traditional alloys.
The superior tribo-corrosion resistance of CoCrFeMnNi is caused by formation of a stable multi-element oxide film at elevated temperature.
The proposed CoCrFeMnNi alloy is homogenized.
The proposed CoCrFeMnNi alloy is polycrystalline and has a fine-grained microstructure.
Combined exposure to elevated temperature, sliding friction, and a chloride-containing corrosive environment will produce a robust, adherent multi-element oxide layer on CoCrFeMnNi.
The multi-element oxide layer acts as a protective barrier.
The multiple principal elements in CoCrFeMnNi facilitate rapid formation of a uniform oxide film.
The oxide film reduces mechanical wear by limiting direct interaction between the substrate and its environment.
The oxide film reduces corrosion by preventing direct interaction between the substrate and the corrosive medium.
At approximately 600°C in a moderate chloride environment, CoCrFeMnNi will have a lower wear rate than stainless steel tested under identical conditions.
At approximately 600°C in a moderate chloride environment, CoCrFeMnNi will have a lower corrosion rate than stainless steel tested under identical conditions.
Enhanced tribo-corrosion resistance is expected around 600°C and in moderate chloride environments.
The effectiveness of the proposed alloy at lower temperatures or in more aggressive corrosive environments is uncertain.
Long-term data on oxide-film stability under cyclic loading and thermal shock are limited.
Variations in high-entropy-alloy composition may alter the proposed protective mechanism.
